title: Why Many Indians Fail at Retirement Planning: 5 Mistakes to Avoid
description: Many individuals delay retirement planning, missing out on the significant benefits of compounding over time. Failing to account for inflation erodes the purc.

faq.q: What is compounding and why is it important for retirement?
faq.a: Compounding is the process where your investment returns also start earning returns. It's crucial for retirement because it allows your wealth to grow exponentially over long periods, making an early start highly beneficial.

faq.q: How much should I save for retirement?
faq.a: There's no one-size-fits-all answer. It depends on your desired retirement lifestyle, current expenses, expected inflation, and investment returns. A common thumb rule suggests aiming for a corpus 20-30 times your annual expenses.

faq.q: Should I only invest in EPF for retirement?
faq.a: While EPF is a good base, it's often not sufficient on its own. Supplementing it with other instruments like mutual funds (equity and debt), NPS, and PPF can help build a more robust and diversified retirement corpus.

faq.q: How often should I review my retirement plan?
faq.a: It's advisable to review your retirement plan at least once a year, or whenever there's a major life event like a job change, marriage, or birth of a child, to ensure it remains aligned with your goals.

faq.q: What role does health insurance play in retirement planning?
faq.a: Health insurance is critical to cover rising medical expenses in old age, preventing your retirement corpus from being depleted by unforeseen health crises. It's essential to have a plan that extends into your retirement years.

faq.q: Can I change my NPS investment options?
faq.a: Yes, NPS allows subscribers to change their asset allocation and Pension Fund Managers (PFMs) periodically, providing flexibility to adapt to changing market conditions and personal preferences.
